title: Cap. V open + Obj. 1: election is love unto salvation — therefore from foresight of faith
latin: Cap. V. Objectiones quaedam Arminianae a Collocutoribus omissae ponuntur et dissolvuntur. Alia apud Arminium occurrunt nonnulla alia argumenta, quae in Collatione Hagiensi non adhibentur; nos ea quoque in medium afferemus, et sigillatim pertractabimus. Ejus generis quamplurima afferuntur in Examine Praedestinationis Perkinsianae; nonnulla alibi: quae uti sese nobis offerent discutiemus. Obj. 1. Electio est amor ad salutem: Deus non potest peccatorem amare ad salutem nisi ipsi sit reconciliatus: Non autem reconciliatur Deus nisi ei quem ut credentem in Christum intuetur: Ergo Deus neminem eligit nisi ex antecedaneo fidei intuitu.
pass_a: Chapter V. Certain Arminian objections omitted by the Collocutors are set forth and dissolved. There occur besides in Arminius some other arguments, which are not employed in the Hague Conference; we will also bring these into the midst, and treat them one by one. Very many of that kind are brought forward in the Examination of the Perkinsian Predestination; some elsewhere: which as they offer themselves to us we will discuss. Objection 1. Election is love unto salvation: God cannot love a sinner unto salvation unless he be reconciled to him: But God is not reconciled except to him whom he looks upon as believing in Christ: Therefore God elects no one except from an antecedent intuition of faith.
pass_b: Cap. V. Certain Arminian objections the Collocutors left out are set out and answered. Arminius has further arguments not used at the Hague Conference; we bring those in too and treat them one by one — many from his Examination of Perkinsian Predestination, some elsewhere. Obj. 1. Election is love unto salvation. God cannot love a sinner unto salvation unless reconciled to him. But God is reconciled only to one he looks on as believing in Christ. Therefore God elects no one except from an antecedent intuition of faith.

title: Cap. V Obj. 1 Sol: election is eternal purpose — love in the electing One, not yet poured out
latin: Sol. Electio est aeternum propositum sive decretum assumendi quosdam homines, aliis praeteritis, ad efficacem et infallibilem gratiae gloriaeque consecutionem: atque hoc sensu recte dicitur Amor ad salutem: Non amor in effectu externo adhuc effusus in electum, sed amor in proposito aeterno adhuc inclusus in ipso eligente. Sic Paulum nondum natum, nedum conversum aut credentem, Deus complectebatur suo arcano amore, habens scilicet in sese aeternum et immutabile propositum gratiam gloriamque eidem impertiendi. Transeat ergo illa prima propositio, Electionem esse amorem ad salutem.
pass_a: Solution. Election is the eternal purpose or decree of assuming certain men, others being passed by, to the efficacious and infallible attainment of grace and glory: and in this sense it is rightly called Love unto salvation: Not love in an external effect already poured out upon the elect, but love in an eternal purpose still enclosed in the electing One himself. Thus Paul not yet born, much less converted or believing, God embraced with his secret love, having namely in himself an eternal and immutable purpose of imparting grace and glory to the same. Let that first proposition therefore pass, that Election is love unto salvation.
pass_b: Sol. Election is the eternal purpose or decree to take certain men, others passed by, to the efficacious infallible attainment of grace and glory — and in that sense it is rightly Love unto salvation: not love already poured out outwardly on the elect, but love still enclosed in the eternal purpose in the electing One himself. So God embraced Paul not yet born, much less converted or believing, with his secret love, having in himself an eternal immutable purpose to impart grace and glory to him. Let the first proposition pass: election is love unto salvation.

title: Cap. V Obj. 1 Sol: cannot love unless reconciled — slippery and false; loves to gift faith
latin: Quae attexuntur, scilicet, Deum non posse praedicto modo ad salutem amare quenquam nisi reconciliatum; reconciliari autem non posse cuiquam nisi ex antecedanea fidei ejus praevisione, sunt valde lubrica, imo manifeste falsa. Nam hoc amore, qui in electionis decreto latere intelligitur, Deus amat nondum reconciliatum eatenus ut illum sibi reconciliandum statuat; amat nondum fidelem, eatenus ut eum fide donandum decernat: quamvis non eo modo amet quo filios suos jam adoptatos, reconciliatos et credentes.
pass_a: The things which are attached, namely, that God cannot in the aforesaid manner love anyone unto salvation unless reconciled; but cannot be reconciled to anyone except from antecedent foresight of his faith, are very slippery, nay manifestly false. For by this love, which is understood to lie hidden in the decree of election, God loves one not yet reconciled so far as to appoint him to be reconciled to himself; he loves one not yet faithful so far as to decree him to be gifted with faith: although he does not love in that manner in which he loves his sons already adopted, reconciled, and believing.
pass_b: What they attach — that God cannot so love anyone unto salvation unless reconciled, and cannot be reconciled to anyone except from antecedent foresight of his faith — is very slippery, indeed plainly false. By the love latent in the election decree, God loves one not yet reconciled so far as to appoint him to be reconciled; loves one not yet faithful so far as to decree him gifted with faith — though not as he loves sons already adopted, reconciled, and believing.

lemmas.gloss: loves to reconcile and gift faith

title: Cap. V Obj. 1 Sol: Arminius's own definition — faith prepared in predestination before foresight
latin: Ipse Arminius, si sibi constare vellet, non posset inficias ire, Deum hoc amore electionis sive praedestinationis complecti electos et praedestinatos ante omnem fidei in illis praevisionem. Nam in Disputationibus publicis, Thes. 15, De praedestinatione, pag. 153, praedestinationem sic definit, Est decretum beneplaciti Dei in Christo quo apud se ab aeterno statuit fideles, quos fide donare decrevit, justificare, adoptare, vita aeterna donare, &c. Et in Examine Praedest. Perkins. concedit Deum non praescire homines crediturus priusquam praedestinaverit ut credant, pag. 32. Atque adjungit hanc rationem optimam sane et validissimam, Praescivit enim, inquit, eos suo dono crediturus, quod donum in praedestinatione praeparatum est, pag. 37. Atque huc etiam spectat quod alibi materiam praedestinationis duplicem ponit: Res divinas (quae benedictionum spiritualium nomine continentur) et personas quibus illarum communicatio est hoc decreto praedestinata. Quaero, Quomodo Deus eligit et praedestinat ex praevisa hominum fide, si in ipsa electione sive praedestinatione donum fidei sit hominibus decretum et praeparatum? Ridiculum est enim dicere, Deum in electione decernere et praeparare fidem certis hominibus, et tamen eosdem homines eligere ex antecedente intuitu fidei hanc ipsam electionem praecedentis; quasi Deus tum demum decerneret donum fidei huic aut illi singulari personae, quando antea perspexerit illum crediturum.
pass_a: Arminius himself, if he wished to be consistent with himself, could not deny that God by this love of election or predestination embraces the elect and predestinated before all foresight of faith in them. For in the Public Disputations, Thesis 15, On predestination, p. 153, he defines predestination thus: It is the decree of the good pleasure of God in Christ by which he has from eternity determined with himself to justify, adopt, gift with eternal life, &c., the faithful whom he has decreed to gift with faith. And in the Examination of the Perkinsian Predestination he grants that God does not foreknow men as about to believe before he has predestinated them that they may believe, p. 32. And he adds this reason, excellent indeed and most valid: For he foreknew, he says, that they would believe by his gift, which gift is prepared in predestination, p. 37. And hither also looks that elsewhere he puts a double matter of predestination: Divine things (which are contained under the name of spiritual blessings) and persons to whom the communication of those is predestinated by this decree. I ask, How does God elect and predestinate from foresight of men's faith, if in election or predestination itself the gift of faith is decreed and prepared for men? For it is ridiculous to say that God in election decrees and prepares faith for certain men, and yet elects the same men from an antecedent intuition of faith preceding this very election; as if God then at last decreed the gift of faith to this or that singular person, when beforehand he had perceived that he would believe.
pass_b: Arminius himself, if consistent, could not deny that by this election/predestination love God embraces the elect before all foresight of faith in them. In Public Disputations, Thesis 15 On predestination (p. 153), he defines: it is God's good-pleasure decree in Christ by which from eternity he determined to justify, adopt, and gift eternal life to the faithful whom he decreed to gift with faith. In the Examination of Perkinsian Predestination he grants God does not foreknow men as about to believe before he has predestinated them to believe (p. 32), and adds the strong reason: he foreknew they would believe by his gift, which gift is prepared in predestination (p. 37). Elsewhere he puts a double matter of predestination: divine things (spiritual blessings) and the persons to whom their communication is predestinated. I ask: how does God elect from foresight of faith if in election itself the gift of faith is decreed and prepared for men? It is ridiculous to say he decrees and prepares faith for certain men in election, yet elects them from an antecedent intuition of faith preceding that election — as if he only then decreed the gift of faith to this or that person when he had already seen he would believe.

lemmas.gloss: gift of faith prepared in predestination

title: Cap. V Obj. 1 Sol close: distinct decrees still; love unto salvation prepares faith for not-yet-believers
latin: Ut hoc incommodum vitaret Arminius, contendit non esse unum decretum quo statuit Deus, Volo fideli dare vitam, et, Volo huic dare fidem, sed distincta. Si sint distincta decreta, cur ipse Arminius in definitionem praedestinationis utrumque confecit? Porro, sint distincta (de quo nos minime laboramus) tamen cum sit praedestinatio sive electio certarum personarum ad fidem, necesse est ut haec electio praecedat omnem fidei intuitum in electis; necesse est ex amore oriatur hisce destinante quod aliis non decernitur. Denique, cum Deus ad fidem elegit singulares personas aliis praeteritis, manifestum est id eum non fecisse inscitum quod haec fides ad vitam aeternam infallibiliter obtinendam conducere; sed hoc potius donum Dei in hunc ipsum finem illis ordinasse et donasse. Exseruit igitur se amor ad salutem erga nondum credentes, praedestinando et praeparando illis donum fidei, quo mediante crederent, credentesque vitam aeternam adirent. Et sic videtis primam hanc objectionem Arminianam nullas vires habere.
pass_a: That he might avoid this inconvenience Arminius contends that it is not one decree by which God establishes, I will give life to the faithful, and, I will give faith to this one, but distinct. If they are distinct decrees, why has Arminius himself put both together in the definition of predestination? Further, let them be distinct (about which we labor least) yet since there is a predestination or election of certain persons to faith, it is necessary that this election precede every intuition of faith in the elect; it is necessary that it arise from love destinating to these what is not decreed to others. Finally, since God has elected singular persons to faith, others being passed by, it is plain that he has not done this unaware that this faith would conduce to obtaining eternal life infallibly; but rather that he has ordained and gifted this gift of God to them unto this very end. Love unto salvation has therefore put itself forth toward those not yet believing, by predestinating and preparing for them the gift of faith, by means of which they might believe, and believing enter eternal life. And so you see that this first Arminian objection has no strength.
pass_b: To dodge the inconvenience Arminius claims there are not one but distinct decrees — I will give life to the faithful, and I will give faith to this one. If distinct, why did he himself put both in his definition of predestination? Let them be distinct (we care little): still, since there is predestination or election of certain persons to faith, that election must precede every intuition of faith in the elect; it must arise from love destinating to these what is not decreed to others. And when God elects singular persons to faith, others passed by, he does not do it unaware that this faith leads infallibly to eternal life — rather he ordained and gifted them that gift unto that end. So love unto salvation puts itself forth toward not-yet-believers by predestinating and preparing the gift of faith whereby they believe and, believing, enter eternal life. Thus this first Arminian objection has no force.

lemmas.lemma: amor ad salutem erga nondum credentes
